# DSH Mindmap

A persistent Excalidraw canvas for DSH
where agents draw alongside you: draw a box, say what goes in

it, and an agent
takes the box, while a lead agent plans how the boxes work together.
*Six boxes, each asked only "<continent> (see note)". The agents agree on one projection between the
mselves and draw a single world map, from memory, in under six minutes.*
Needs DSH 0.2.x with its Agent Teams plugin. MIT licensed.
## Install

**Plugins page** (DSH Web or Desktop): open **Plugins** in the sidebar and turn
on **Agent Teams**.
Then choose **Add plugin**, paste this address and install:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
**Terminal** (a CLI Web profile):
[代码示例省略，未执行]

**Ask an agent**: paste this into DSH (Creator mode), Claude Code, Codex or any
coding agent:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

Then open **Mindmap** in the sidebar, pick a workspace and create a canvas.
Press **F**, drag a box,
type what it should hold and press Enter.
## What a canvas brings

Besides the usual drawing tools (notes, text, shapes, arrows, drag, marquee
select, zoom, undo/redo,

usual drawing tools (notes, text, shapes, arrows, drag, marquee
select, zoom, undo/redo, autosave):

- **A lead**: every canvas is one DSH Session, shown under the canvas. Talk to
it there; it is the T

eam Lead of the agents working on the canvas.
- **Smart boxes**: a box is an Excalidraw frame (the *

*F** tool). Elements it
covers belong to it. Draw a box and say what it should hold: a new teammate

of the lead takes the box, locked to it.
- **Locks**: a locked box, and everything lying in it, can

be changed only by
its holder, the user or one agent. Boxes may overlap; what lies in the
overlap st
ays locked to both holders.

Dependencies, relays and conflicts between agents are not a canvas mechanism:
the lead and its teamm

ates settle them with Agent Teams (messages, the task
board), as a team working in one workspace doe

s. Scheduling stays with DSH's
automation tasks.
## Using it

- **Talk to the lead** in the chat under the canvas; drag its top edge to
resize it.
- **Give a box

to an agent**: press **F**, drag a box, type what it should
make and press Enter (Esc keeps a plain

box). A selected box without an
agent offers **Ask an agent** the same way.
- **Talk to a box's agen

t**: select its box or click its chip; the chat
switches to that teammate. The tabs above the chat s

witch back. Talking is
how you steer an agent: what you draw on the canvas stays yours, never taken

as an instruction or moved, and an agent hears what you changed in or beside
its box the next time i

t looks. Stopping an agent, deleting its work or
lifting its lock are decisions the lead respects.
-

**Watch agents work**: each agent at work shows as a collaborator cursor
where it last read or drew

, saying what it does or what it tells a teammate
(dots while it thinks), with what it just changed

outlined. Click its avatar
at the top right to go there.
- **Locks**: select a box and **Lock** it t

o keep agents out; click a lock
chip to lift any lock, yours or an agent's.
## Agent tools

The lead Session of a canvas, its teammates and the helpers they start get three
tools and a short c

anvas policy; other Sessions in the workspace get neither, nor
any mention of the canvases. The poli

cy covers how to work on a canvas (claim and
lock a box before drawing, message the holder instead o

f working around a lock,
let the drawing be the report and message others only when they must act, u

se only
these tools on canvases). Their descriptions, schemas and errors are the whole
contract.
| Tool | Purpose |
| `canvas_read` | Who you are on the canvas, its boxes with owner and lock holder, and elements as c

ompact Excalidraw JSON, for the canvas, one box or chosen ids. |
| `canvas_view` | A PNG of the canv

as, a box, ids or a region, drawn like the canvas, with optional coordinate grid. |
| `canvas_write`
| One atomic batch of creations, partial updates (by `id`), group moves and copies (placed, scaled
and turned as a whole), restacking (`above`/`below`), deletions and box locks (`"lock": true/false`)
turned as a whole), restacking (`above`/`below`), deletions and box locks (`"lock": true/false`). |

An agent locking a box becomes its owner, as does a teammate locking a box the
lead drew for it. Onl

y the holder changes a locked box; the canvas lead may lift
a teammate's lock (locking the box again

gives it back to the teammate), and
only the user lifts a lock the user set. Helpers an agent start

s write as that
agent.

## Configuration
Set these on the `mindmap` entry in the profile's `cordis.patch.yml`:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
| Option | Default | Meaning |
| `fontFiles` | `[]` | Font files used for images agents see, such as a CJK face. Empty uses the fir
st installed CJK system font. CJK text in Excalifont, the default font, is drawn with Excalidraw's o

wn Xiaolai instead. |
| `teammateProvider` | `spawn` | The subagent provider a box's teammate starts
with, as Agent Teams uses for fresh teammates. |
## Development
[代码示例省略，未执行]

To try a checkout, add it to a profile with
`dsh plugin --profile web add link:$PWD` and rebuild aft

er changes. A release
attaches the built `npm pack` tarball as `dsh-mindmap-<version>.tgz`; update
t
he address under Install to match.

`client.js` registers the page and its embedded conversation;
`client.canvas.js` (Excalidraw) loads

on first visit. `index.js` is the Host
plugin: `src/host/` holds the canvas store, lock and write ru

les, the canvas
team, tools, routes and the PNG renderer; `src/shared/` is used by both sides.
